_: Pattern rules for the plugin safety scan. Used by tools/store.py and by the vrfrida app (it downloads this file with the store index). Regexes must work in both Python re and Java regex (no lookbehind, no named groups). sev: high | medium | low. own_game_ok: a hit is ignored when the line names one of the plugin's own games (its // game: line) or APP_ID.

rules.label: Opens its own internet connections (Java networking)
rules.why: Plugins almost never need this. It is how stolen data gets sent out.

rules.label: Uses raw sockets (connect / send / socket)
rules.why: Low-level networking that skips the game. Common in data stealers.

rules.label: Uses Frida's Socket API
rules.why: Lets the script talk to any server directly.

rules.label: Makes web requests (UnityWebRequest / WWW / fetch)
rules.why: Fine for loading pictures, but check WHERE it sends data and WHAT it sends.

rules.label: Mentions a webhook / paste / file-drop service
rules.why: Discord webhooks, Telegram bots and paste sites are the usual places stolen tokens get sent.

rules.label: Contains a raw IP address URL
rules.why: Real services use domain names; a bare IP is often a private collection server.

rules.label: Runs shell commands / other programs
rules.why: A game plugin has no reason to run commands on your headset.

rules.label: Runs code it builds or downloads at runtime (eval / new Function / Script.load)
rules.why: The code you read is not the code that runs. Can pull in anything later.

rules.label: Reads accounts / auth tokens
rules.why: Can take over your Meta or game account.

rules.label: Touches login / session / password data
rules.why: Can be legit (e.g. reading your own player id), but check it never leaves the device.

rules.label: Reads other apps' private folders
rules.why: /data/data and /data/user hold other apps' logins and saves. (Paths that name the plugin's own game are not counted.)

rules.label: Writes or deletes files
rules.why: Settings files are normal; deleting or writing outside the game's folder is not.

rules.label: Starts other apps / installs packages
rules.why: Can open pages, install apps or send intents outside the game.

rules.label: Looks obfuscated (_0x names)
rules.why: javascript-obfuscator output. Hidden code is a big red flag in a free plugin.

rules.label: Long runs of escaped characters (\x.. / \u....)
rules.why: Used to hide strings like URLs from people reading the code.

rules.label: Huge encoded blob (base64 / hex) in a string
rules.why: Could be a picture, or hidden code that gets decoded and run.

rules.label: Builds strings from character codes / decodes base64
rules.why: Sometimes normal, sometimes used to hide URLs.

rules.label: Writes native memory / patches code
rules.why: Normal for mods (that's how most cheats work). Listed so you know it's there.

rules.label: Touches currency / purchases
rules.why: Writing paid currency or faking purchases can get accounts banned.

rules.label: Mentions crash / lag-all / kick features
rules.why: Lobby-wide crash or lag features ruin games for everyone and get you banned.
